took: Cadence, health board and budget checks all cleared ($0 gates_verdict.py + stuck_clock.py reads fed into health.py --check for a fully-measured board rather than the UNMEASURED default). Re-scored the queue, claimed the top free unowned item, AUT-PROP-064 (172.9, RT-VTE-PROPHYLAXIS's remaining required_validation item). Rung-0 (WebSearch) gave a plausible answer but rung-0b verification (WebFetch on pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov, nejm.org, ebi.ac.uk) was EGRESS_BLOCKED from this sandbox, so escalated to rung 1 per ci-escape-hatches: dispatched .github/workflows/fetch-literature.yml (run 33821316750) rather than write an unverified identifier. The run's own known-positive control (PMID 30511879) matched, confirming the query actually retrieved the AVERT trial rather than nothing. Read the retrieved corpus (950 files on literature-cache) for the two named trials the item's next_action pointed at (AVERT/CASSINI class).
what_changed: AUT-PROP-064 asked for a fetched, cited overall-survival result from an ambulatory-cancer VTE-prophylaxis trial -- explicitly not from recollection. Retrieved and read AVERT (Carrier et al., NEJM 2019, PMID 30511879): apixaban reduced VTE events (4.2% vs 10.2%, HR 0.41) but increased major bleeding (HR 2.00); the trial's own abstract carries no all-cause mortality figure, so also read a published secondary source in full text (Song et al. 2019, PMC6593743, open access) which states explicitly 'no difference in non-major bleeding or mortality' for AVERT. Read CASSINI (Khorana et al., NEJM 2019, PMID 30786186): the composite VTE-or-VTE-death endpoint was NOT significantly reduced over the full 180-day trial period (HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.40-1.09, p=0.10) -- only during the on-treatment intervention window (HR 0.40). The route's registered prediction (event-rate reduction without a survival gain) is CONFIRMED by real trial evidence rather than carried as an assumption. Registered three new evidence entries (EV-CARRIER-2019, EV-KHORANA-2019, EV-SONG-2019) in systems/graph/evidence.json with full citations, PMIDs/DOIs and provenance flags naming the dispatch that retrieved them. Wrote the finding into RT-VTE-PROPHYLAXIS's rationale, supporting_evidence, remaining_unknowns, readiness and next in systems/graph/routes.json; required_validation item 2 is now answered (item 1 was already done by the prior cycle; item 3 remains blocked on BLK-NO-EMC-DATA). Regenerated systems/views/ (systems_check.py --write-views). Hit one process hiccup: the dev branch named in this session's instructions (claude/quirky-johnson-vcptxy) was 66 commits behind origin/main and the research-loop skill's explicit instruction is to push to main directly, so switched to main, which produced a merge conflict in research-ledger.json against concurrent cycles' writes -- resolved by resetting the ledger to origin/main's current state and re-running priority.py plus a targeted, minimal write-back to only the AUT-PROP-064 row (never a blind full-ledger overwrite, to avoid clobbering concurrent sessions).
cost: $0 -- free. One GitHub Actions dispatch (fetch-literature.yml, ~13 min wall clock, CI runner, no Claude plan budget), two WebSearch calls, three blocked WebFetch attempts (no cost, egress-blocked), local reads/greps against the fetched corpus, two preflight runs (one stale, superseded by the second which ran on the settled post-merge tree and reported PREFLIGHT OK against PINNED_SHA=14a3f172d...+dirty matching the committed tree).
